record.paper_title: Developments, Applications and Open Problems in Fixed Point Theory
record.original_question: A Banach space X has the weak fixed point property (WFPP) when every weakly compact convex subset K of X has the fixed point property: every nonexpansive self-map T: K -> K, meaning ||T x - T y|| <= ||x - y|| for all x,y in K, has at least one fixed point in K. Is it true that every Banach space has the weak fixed point property?

evidence.quote: A mapping T: K -> K is said to be nonexpansive if ||Tx - Ty|| <= ||x - y|| for all x,y in K. We define K as possessing the fixed point property (FPP) if each nonexpansive map defined on K has a fixed point within K. Moreover, we define X as having the FPP if every closed bounded convex subset of X possesses the FPP, and X has the weak FPP if each weakly compact convex subset of X has the FPP.
For quite some time, a lingering question persisted: Does every Banach space have the WFPP? In 1981, Alspach provided the initial and essentially sole known instance of a space lacking the WFPP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|$. A subset $K\subseteq X$ is said to have the fixed point property (FPP) if every nonexpansive self-map $T:K\to K$ (i.e., a map satisfying $\|Tx-Ty\|\le\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in K$) admits at least one fixed point in $K$. The space $X$ is said to have the weak fixed point property (WFPP) if every weakly compact convex subset $K\subseteq X$ has the FPP.

Question: Does every Banach space have the weak fixed point property?
artifact.category_tag: Fixed point property in Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved in the negative. In 1981, D. Alspach constructed a weakly compact convex subset of $L^1[0,1]$ and a fixed-point-free nonexpansive self-map, providing an example of a Banach space without the weak fixed point property.

status_evidence.title: A fixed point free nonexpansive map (Alspach, 1981)
status_evidence.snippet: Alspach exhibits a weakly compact convex subset of L^1[0,1] and a nonexpansive map of it into itself without a fixed point.
status_evidence.claim: Not every Banach space has the WFPP; L^1[0,1] is a counterexample.
